To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the universal scheme ξ, which is computable, predicts the next symbol of an unknown environment with the same accuracy as the best possible informed scheme, and (2) this is the best that can be done with a computable prediction scheme.

the average number (or the probability) of prediction errors made in the universal scheme ξ rapidly converges to the average number (probability) of prediction errors of the best possible informed prediction scheme for any computable environment µ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and investigation of computable prediction schemes which are optimal in a universal sense.
the fundamental problem of how to predict the future in an unknown, but computable probabilistic world.
the development of computable universal schemes and their convergence properties for prediction and related tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
universal prediction of arbitrary sequences by arbitrary computable prediction schemes is a very well behaved problem.
Solomonoff's universal prediction scheme is the best computable prediction scheme, and it is the best computably computable prediction scheme.
the universal prediction scheme ξ is a very useful tool for the analysis of the performance of any prediction scheme in any given environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it provides an information theoretic foundation for prediction and classification of arbitrary sequences by a computable system.
we are now able to give a rigorous mathematical foundation for the universal prediction scheme ξ, and to quantify its performance in a variety of situations.

we have shown that the universal prediction scheme ξ can be used for universal prediction of nonbinary sequences and that it converges to the best possible prediction in a conditional mean-squared error sense.
The main takeaway from our work is that
universal prediction schemes can be designed to converge to the best possible informed scheme, even if the environment is unknown.
the universal prediction schemes can achieve a performance close to the best informed scheme in many practical scenarios.
